name: MGM Transformers (a Forgent company)
old_description: Dry-type and liquid-filled distribution/power transformers (cast coil, VPI, padmount)
about:
MGM Transformers, headquartered in Vernon, California, traces its origins to 1926 and has operated under the MGM name since 1974. Now a subsidiary of Forgent, the company designs and manufactures transformers for power distribution across North America.

The company produces dry-type transformers — including vacuum pressure impregnated (VPI) and cast coil designs — as well as liquid-filled padmount and substation units. It also builds custom power distribution unit (PDU) transformers for high-density data centers and general-purpose low-voltage transformers. Manufacturing is vertically integrated across five facilities totaling 1.5 million square feet in California, Texas, and Tijuana, Mexico, with a workforce of approximately 1,500 employees.

MGM serves data center operators (from hyperscale to edge), solar and renewable energy developers, commercial and industrial facilities, utilities, and industrial manufacturing plants. Its transformers are specified for grid modernization projects, including utility-scale solar, storage, and substation infrastructure. A noted example is Standard Solar, which received a grounding transformer in four weeks to restore site operations.

The company emphasizes vertically integrated manufacturing, industry-leading lead times, and a rush-order program (Bull Rush) for urgent needs. It stocks transformers in 20 major U.S. cities for rapid deployment and reports a 98% on-time delivery rate across a $4 billion installed base.
